claim.speaker: P. Chidambaram
claim.quote_original: In the current year too, according to the Advance Estimates by the Central Statistical Organisation (CSO), the growth rate will be 8.7 per cent - although I am confident that we will maintain the average of 8.8 per cent.
claim.quote_english: In the current year too, according to the Advance Estimates by the Central Statistical Organisation (CSO), the growth rate will be 8.7 per cent - although I am confident that we will maintain the average of 8.8 per cent.
claim.summary: The Finance Minister projected 8.8% GDP growth for 2008-09; revised national accounts data show 6.7%.
claim.analysis:
Chidambaram's 2008-09 Budget speech projected 8.7% growth for the year and said he was confident of maintaining the 8.8% average of the previous four years. The projection was made before the full impact of the global financial crisis.

The Economic Survey 2008-09, using revised CSO estimates, put 2008-09 GDP growth at 6.7%, 2.1 percentage points below the 8.8% average of the preceding five years. In May 2008 the Finance Minister had also said growth would be 'not less than 8.5%'.

The outturn was below both the Budget projection and the later 8.5% floor. The survey identifies the global crisis and a sharp deceleration in agriculture, manufacturing and construction as the main factors.
claim.notes: Budget speech from indiabudget.gov.in. Actual growth from Economic Survey 2008-09 revised estimates.

claim.speaker: Pranab Mukherjee
claim.quote_original: I expect India's GDP growth in 2012-13 to be 7.6 per cent, +/- 0.25 per cent.
claim.quote_english: I expect India's GDP growth in 2012-13 to be 7.6 per cent, +/- 0.25 per cent.
claim.summary: The Finance Minister projected 7.6% GDP growth for 2012-13; the advance estimate was 5.0%.

govt_response.title: PIB: Budget 2012-13 summary notes global crisis
govt_response.summary: The Finance Ministry said the global crisis had affected India but that India remained among the front runners in economic growth.

claim.analysis:
Pranab Mukherjee's 2012-13 Budget speech projected GDP growth of 7.6% +/- 0.25% for the year, after 6.9% growth in 2011-12. The projection assumed a recovery in industrial investment.

The CSO's advance estimate for 2012-13, reported in the Economic Survey 2012-13, put growth at 5.0%. Later revisions on the 2004-05 base put it at 4.5%; on the 2011-12 base the figure is 5.5%.

The outturn was 2.1 to 2.6 percentage points below the lower bound of the Budget projection.
claim.notes: Budget speech PDF from indiabudget.gov.in. Actual from Economic Survey 2012-13; later revisions differ by base year.

claim.speaker: P. Chidambaram
claim.quote_original: Red lines were drawn for the fiscal deficit at 5.3 percent of GDP this year and 4.8 percent of GDP in 2013-14.
claim.quote_english: Red lines were drawn for the fiscal deficit at 5.3 percent of GDP this year and 4.8 percent of GDP in 2013-14.
claim.summary: The Budget set a 4.8%-of-GDP fiscal deficit red line for 2013-14; provisional data show 4.5%.

govt_response.title: Interim Budget 2014-15: fiscal deficit below the red line
govt_response.summary: The Finance Minister said the 2013-14 fiscal deficit would be contained at 4.6% of GDP, below the 4.8% red line.

claim.analysis:
The 2013-14 Budget set a fiscal-deficit red line of 4.8% of GDP, down from 5.2% in 2012-13. The Finance Minister said the red lines were a promise he would not cross.

The Economic Survey 2013-14 reports the provisional fiscal deficit for 2013-14 at 4.5% of GDP. The interim Budget of February 2014 put the revised estimate at 4.6%, below the 4.8% line.

The outcome was within the target. The survey attributes the improvement mainly to expenditure compression rather than higher revenue.
claim.notes: The 4.8% figure was both a Budget estimate and a red-line commitment. Provisional actual 4.5%; revised estimate 4.6%.

claim.speaker: Sonia Gandhi
claim.quote_original: Average growth in the first four years of the Congress-led UPA government was 9% per year for the first time in our history.
claim.quote_english: Average growth in the first four years of the Congress-led UPA government was 9% per year for the first time in our history.
claim.summary: The 2009 Congress manifesto said UPA growth averaged 9% a year in its first four years; official data put the average at about 8.8-9.1%.

transcript_sources.title: Indian National Congress, Lok Sabha Elections 2009 Manifesto (PDF)

evidence.title: Indian National Congress, Lok Sabha Elections 2009 Manifesto
evidence.key_figure: Average growth in the first four years of the UPA government: 9% per year.

claim.analysis:
The 2009 Congress manifesto stated that average growth in the first four years of the UPA government was 9% per year. The Economic Survey 2008-09 reports GDP growth of 8.5%, 7.5%, 9.5% and 9.7% for 2004-05 to 2007-08 on the series used in that survey, an average of about 8.8%.

Other vintages of the national accounts put the four-year average at about 9.1%. The manifesto's 9% figure is a rounded representation of those estimates.

The claim is consistent with the official growth data available in 2009, within rounding.
claim.notes: Manifesto text from the 2009 PDF. The 9% figure is a rounded average; different national-accounts vintages give about 8.8-9.1%.
